A cross-section of the Earth showing a wedge cut out, similar to a slice of cake. The layers are clearly marked from the centre outwards: Inner Core (solid sphere at the tip), Outer Core (liquid layer), Mantle (thickest middle layer), and Crust (very thin outermost line). Enlarged detail of the crust showing the thicker Continental Crust (Sial) forming land, sitting above the thinner Oceanic Crust (Sima) under the ocean. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Split diagram contrasting the forces. Top half (Compressional): Two arrows pointing inwards towards a block of layered rock, which is buckled into a wavy shape. Bottom half (Tensional): Two arrows pointing outwards away from a block of rock. The rock is cracked by two diagonal lines, and the middle block has slid downwards. Labels: "Tensional force", "Normal faults", "Rift Valley (Graben)", "Block Mountains (Horsts)" on the sides. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Cross-section of a Karst limestone cave. Rainwater is shown infiltrating from the grassy surface through cracks (swallow holes). Inside the dark cavern, cone-shaped rock formations hang from the ceiling (Stalactites). Water drips from them onto upward-pointing cones on the floor (Stalagmites). On the left, a stalactite and stalagmite have joined to form a thick vertical column (Pillar). An underground river flows at the base. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
